    --only C-UNIT,C-TRANSCRIPTS,C-SEP-TERMS,C-EMU-PIN,C-CLEAN-FOLDER,C-FWTEST-PIN) > "$work/inside.log" 2>&1 \
    || { cat "$work/inside.log"; bad "the firmware side's checks failed inside the clean folder"; }
grep -E '^C-' "$work/inside.log" | sed 's/^/inside:   /'
if GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$clean" log -p "$base..HEAD" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "git log -p: needed no excluded file"
else
    echo "git log -p: refused to fetch excluded files, as it should"
fi
no_blobs "after the tools and git log -p"

# An update from HEAD's parent to HEAD.
if parent=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse -q --verify "HEAD~1"); then
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/old "$parent"
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/main "$head"
    SETUP_SOURCE="file://$work/src.git" SETUP_REF=old \
        sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" "$work/clean2" > /dev/null 2>&1 || bad "clean-setup.sh at HEAD's parent failed"
    if sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-update.sh" --dir "$work/clean2" main > "$work/update.log" 2>&1; then
        echo "update:   $(tail -1 "$work/update.log")"
    else
        cat "$work/update.log"; bad "tools/clean-update.sh failed"
    fi
    clean_saved=$clean; clean="$work/clean2"
    [ "$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$head" ] || bad "the update did not reach HEAD"
    for p in $EXCLUDED; do [ ! -e "$clean/$p" ] || bad "$p is on disk after the update"; done
    no_blobs "after an update"
    clean=$clean_saved
fi

if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "clean folder: PASS"; else echo "clean folder: FAIL"; fi
exit $fail
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Archives a finished session's transcript into sessions/ (R-CLEAN-3).

  archive-session.py TRANSCRIPT.jsonl --role clean|spec [--out sessions/<role>]

Run it at the start of the next session (never on the live session). A
clean session archives only clean sessions; a spec session may archive
either (sessions/README.md). It copies the transcript to
`sessions/<role>/<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl` (the date is
the UTC date of its first entry), along with any subagent transcripts
(`<id>/subagents/*.jsonl` next to it) into `<same name>.subagents/`. It
redacts:
  - tokens and keys (GitHub, Anthropic, AWS, bearer tokens, private keys);
  - e-mail addresses, except no-reply addresses;
  - account and organisation IDs;
  - private paths: home folders become `~`, and per-user temp folders are
    shortened;
  - the local user names seen in those paths, wherever they appear, and
    `*.local` host names.
It writes `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md` beside the copy, saying what was
redacted and how many times, with the SHA-256 of the original and of the
copy. Every redacted line must still parse as JSON. It refuses to overwrite
an existing archive.
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import glob
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import sys

RULES = [
    ("private key", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----.*?-----END[A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY-----"),
     "[REDACTED:private-key]"),
    ("GitHub token", re.compile(r"\b(gh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}|github_pat_[A-Za-z0-9_]{20,})"),
     "[REDACTED:github-token]"),
    ("Anthropic key", re.compile(r"\bsk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}"), "[REDACTED:anthropic-key]"),
    ("AWS key ID", re.compile(r"\b(AKIA|ASIA)[0-9A-Z]{16}\b"), "[REDACTED:aws-key]"),
    ("bearer token", re.compile(r"(?i)\bbearer\s+[A-Za-z0-9._~+/-]{20,}=*"), "Bearer [REDACTED]"),
    ("account or organisation ID",
     re.compile(r'("(?:owner)?(?:[Aa]ccount|[Oo]rganization)(?:Uuid|Id|UUID|_uuid|_id)"\s*:\s*")[^"]+(")'),
     r"\1[REDACTED:account-id]\2"),
    ("e-mail address",
     re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b"),
     "[REDACTED:email]"),
    ("home folder path", re.compile(r"/(?:Users|home)/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(?=/|\b)"), "~"),
    ("per-user temp path", re.compile(r"/private/tmp/claude-\d+/|/tmp/claude-\d+/"), "/tmp/claude-UID/"),
    ("project folder name", re.compile(r"-Users-[A-Za-z0-9._]+-"), "-HOME-"),
]
# no-reply addresses are kept: they identify authors without being private
KEEP_EMAIL = re.compile(r"noreply@|@users\.noreply\.github\.com")


HOST_RULE = ("host name", re.compile(r"\b[A-Za-z0-9-]+\.local\b(?!\.)"), "[REDACTED:host]")
HOME_USER = re.compile(r"/(?:Users|home)/([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)/")


def user_rules(path):
    """Rules for the local user names seen in home-folder paths, so they are
    also redacted where they appear alone (e.g. in `ls -l` output)."""
    names = set()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            names.update(HOME_USER.findall(line))
    names -= {"Shared", "runner"}
    return [("local user name", re.compile(r"\b%s\b" % re.escape(n)), "[REDACTED:user]")
            for n in sorted(names)]


def redact_line(line, counts, extra=()):
    for name, rx, repl in list(RULES) + [HOST_RULE] + list(extra):
        if name == "e-mail address":
            def sub(m):
                if KEEP_EMAIL.search(m.group(0)):
                    return m.group(0)
                counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + 1
                return repl
            line = rx.sub(sub, line)
            continue
        line, n = rx.subn(repl, line)
        if n:
            counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + n
    return line


def redact_file(src, dst, counts, extra=()):
    h_src, h_dst = hashlib.sha256(), hashlib.sha256()
    with open(src, "rb") as f, open(dst, "wb") as out:
        for n, raw in enumerate(f, 1):
            h_src.update(raw)
            line = redact_line(raw.decode("utf-8"), counts, extra)
            if line.strip():
                try:
                    json.loads(line)
                except ValueError as e:
                    raise SystemExit("%s:%d: redaction broke the JSON (%s)" % (src, n, e))
            data = line.encode("utf-8")
            h_dst.update(data)
            out.write(data)
    return h_src.hexdigest(), h_dst.hexdigest()


def first_date(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        for line in f:
            try:
                ts = json.loads(line).get("timestamp")
            except ValueError:
                continue
            if ts:
                return ts[:10]
    return datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__,
                                 formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("transcript")
    ap.add_argument("--role", required=True, choices=("clean", "spec"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=None,
                    help="where to put it (default: sessions/<role>/)")
    ap.add_argument("--archived-by", default="",
                    help="the session doing the archiving, for the note")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.out is None:
        a.out = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                             "sessions", a.role)

    src = a.transcript
    sid = os.path.basename(src)[:-len(".jsonl")]
    name = "%s-%s-%s" % (first_date(src), a.role, sid)
    dst = os.path.join(a.out, name + ".jsonl")
    if os.path.exists(dst):
        raise SystemExit("refusing to overwrite %s" % dst)
    os.makedirs(a.out, exist_ok=True)

    counts = {}
    files = [(src, dst)]
    subs = sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(src), sid, "subagents", "*.jsonl")))
    if subs:
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(a.out, name + ".subagents"))
        files += [(s, os.path.join(a.out, name + ".subagents", os.path.basename(s))) for s in subs]
    extra = []
    for s, _ in files:
        extra += [r for r in user_rules(s) if r[1].pattern not in [e[1].pattern for e in extra]]
    hashes = []
    for s, d in files:
        hs, hd = redact_file(s, d, counts, extra)
        hashes.append((os.path.relpath(d, a.out), hs, hd))

    now = datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
    # REUSE-IgnoreStart
    note = ["<!--", "SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT",
            "SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98", "-->", "",
            # REUSE-IgnoreEnd
            "# Redactions: %s" % name, "",
            "- Session: `%s` (%s side)" % (sid, a.role),
            "- Archived: %s%s" % (now, (" by " + a.archived_by) if a.archived_by else ""),
            "- Tool: tools/archive-session.py (its RULES list is the full redaction policy)",
            "", "## What was redacted", ""]
    if counts:
        note += ["| Kind | Count |", "|------|-------|"]
        note += ["| %s | %d |" % (k, counts[k]) for k in sorted(counts)]
    else:
        note.append("Nothing.")
    note += ["", "Nothing else was changed. Redactions replace text in place, so every line",
             "is still the same JSON entry.", "",
             "## Files", "",
             "| File | SHA-256 of the original | SHA-256 of this copy |",
             "|------|-------------------------|----------------------|"]
    note += ["| `%s` | `%s` | `%s` |" % h for h in hashes]
    note.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(a.out, name + ".REDACTIONS.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(note))
    print("archived %s -> %s" % (src, dst))
    for k in sorted(counts):
        print("  redacted %-28s %d" % (k, counts[k]))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Spec-side text discipline (R-SEP-1, check C-SEP-TERMS).

  check-emulator-terms.py [--show]

Looks for identifiers that occur in vendor/emulator/ and nowhere in
vendor/jieli-sdk/, in the places the firmware side reads:
  - every tracked text file outside vendor/emulator/, harness/, sessions/
    (transcripts), docs/prompts/ (prompts are kept verbatim), and the two
    doors, docs/HARNESS.md and HARDWARE-SPEC.md (reviewed by people);
  - the commit messages in COMMIT_RANGE (default ..HEAD);
  - the pull request's title and body, when GITHUB_EVENT_PATH names one.

The list is built at run time from vendor/emulator/ and never written down:
identifier-shaped words (with an underscore, inner capitals, or letters and
digits mixed; four characters or more, not just hex digits) and hex numbers
of four digits or more. Terms that already occur in CLEAN_BASELINE's tree
(the repository as the clean side left it at the end of M0a, before any
emulator source entered it) or in vendor/jieli-sdk/ are not on the list. A hit is reported as its place and a SHA-256 prefix of the word, never
the word or the text around it, because the log is visible to the firmware
side; `--show` prints the word too, for a spec-side author fixing it. A
reviewed false positive is listed by that hash in
config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json, with a reason that doesn't name it.

Where vendor/emulator/ isn't on disk (a clean folder), it says SKIP.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EMU = os.path.join(ROOT, "vendor", "emulator")
SDK = os.path.join(ROOT, "vendor", "jieli-sdk")
REVIEWED = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "emulator-terms-reviewed.json")
# main at the end of M0a (pull request #2): written by the clean side only
CLEAN_BASELINE = "265f15b5b646cf7d5110d4606365d82fae93f5bc"
EXCLUDE = ("vendor/emulator/", "harness/", "sessions/", "docs/prompts/")
DOORS = ("docs/HARNESS.md", "HARDWARE-SPEC.md", "docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md")

WORD = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9A-Za-z_])[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
HEX = re.compile(r"\b0[xX][0-9A-Fa-f_]{4,}\b")


def shaped(w):
    if len(w) < 4 or not re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", w):
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r"x?[0-9A-Fa-f]+(_[ui](8|16|32|64))?", w):
        return False
    if "_" in w.strip("_"):
        return True
    if re.search(r"[a-z][A-Z]", w):
        return True
    return bool(re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", w) and re.search(r"[0-9]", w))


def norm_hex(h):
    v = int(h[2:].replace("_", ""), 16)
    return "0x%x" % v if v >= 0x1000 else None


def terms_of(text):
    out = set(n for n in (norm_hex(h) for h in HEX.findall(text)) if n)
    out.update(w for w in WORD.findall(HEX.sub(" ", text)) if shaped(w))
    return out


def walk_text(top):
    for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(top):
        for n in names:
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(dirpath, n), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    yield f.read()
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
                continue


def emulator_terms():
    emu = set()
    for text in walk_text(EMU):
        emu |= terms_of(text)
    known = set()
    for text in walk_text(SDK):
        known |= terms_of(text)
    for text in baseline_texts():
        known |= terms_of(text)
    return emu - known


def baseline_texts():
    names = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", CLEAN_BASELINE],
                           check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True).stdout.split()
    for n in names:
        blob = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "show", "%s:%s" % (CLEAN_BASELINE, n)],
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE).stdout
        try:
            yield blob.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue


def h(term):
    return hashlib.sha256(term.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def reviewed():
    if not os.path.exists(REVIEWED):
        return {}
    with open(REVIEWED, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    out = {}
    for r in data.get("reviewed", []):
        if not (r.get("sha256_16") and r.get("reason")):
            raise SystemExit("%s: each entry needs sha256_16 and reason" % REVIEWED)
        out[r["sha256_16"]] = r["reason"]
    return out


def tracked():
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "ls-files", "-z"], check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    return [x.decode() for x in p.stdout.split(b"\0") if x]


def hits_in(text, terms, where):
    found = []
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        for t in terms_of(line) & terms:
            found.append((where, n, t))
    return found


def main():
    show = "--show" in sys.argv[1:]
    if not os.path.isdir(EMU):
        print("SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)")
        return 0
    terms = emulator_terms()
    ok_hashes = reviewed()
    hits = []
    scanned = 0
    for p in tracked():
        if p.startswith(EXCLUDE) or p in DOORS:
            continue
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(ROOT, p), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                text = f.read()
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        scanned += 1
        hits += hits_in(text, terms, p)
    rng = os.environ.get("COMMIT_RANGE") or "..HEAD"
    log = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "log", "--format=%x00%H%n%B", rng],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True).stdout
    commits = [c for c in log.split("\0") if c.strip()]
    for c in commits:
        sha, _, body = c.partition("\n")
        hits += hits_in(body, terms, "commit %s" % sha[:12])
    event = os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")
    pr = 0
    if event and os.path.exists(event):
        with open(event, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            ev = json.load(f)
        pull = ev.get("pull_request") or {}
        if pull:
            pr = 1
            hits += hits_in(pull.get("title") or "", terms, "pull request title")
            hits += hits_in(pull.get("body") or "", terms, "pull request body")
    bad = 0
    for where, n, t in sorted(hits):
        key = h(t)
        if key in ok_hashes:
            print("REVIEWED %s:%d term %s: %s" % (where, n, key, ok_hashes[key]))
            continue
        bad += 1
        print("HIT %s:%d term %s%s" % (where, n, key, (" (%s)" % t) if show else ""))
    print("%d emulator-only terms; %d files, %d commit messages, %d pull request texts scanned"
          % (len(terms), scanned, len(commits), pr))
    print("emulator terms: %s" % ("FAIL" if bad else "PASS"))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""Runs every check and writes the test record (R-PROC-4, R-REC-1).

  record.py run --out DIR [--only C-A,C-B] [--skip C-X] [--with-merge]
      Runs the checks in CHECKS, writes DIR/report.json, DIR/report.md,
      DIR/logs/<check>.log, DIR/outputs/ (the build outputs) and
      DIR/SHA256SUMS (of all of those). Exit status 1 if any check failed.
  record.py compare --record REPORT.json --outputs DIR
      Compares DIR/SHA256SUMS with the outputs listed in a record
      (used by tools/reproduce). Exit status 1 on any difference.

Environment: COMMIT_RANGE (for C-COMMIT-MSG, default: every commit reachable
from HEAD), GITHUB_* (recorded, and used by C-LOW-PROFILE and C-MERGE).
"""
import argparse
import datetime
import hashlib
import json
import os
import platform
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
PY = sys.executable or "python3"
SCHEMA = 1


def _low_profile_cmd():
    if os.environ.get("GITHUB_ACTIONS") == "true":
        return [PY, "-I", "tools/check-low-profile.py", "--require-api"]
    return [PY, "-I", "tools/check-low-profile.py", "--offline"]


def _commit_range():
    return os.environ.get("COMMIT_RANGE") or "..HEAD"


# Each check: id, title, requirement IDs, and either a command (list, or a
# function returning one, run from the repository root) or an internal
# function name. "records_only" checks run only with --with-merge.
CHECKS = [
    {"id": "C-UNIT", "title": "Unit tests of the tools",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1", "R-PROC-4", "R-REC-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-4", "R-PUB-1",
              "R-SEP-2"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-m", "unittest", "discover", "-s", "tests", "-t", ".", "-v"]},
    {"id": "C-REUSE", "title": "reuse lint (SPDX licence and copyright on every file)",
     "reqs": ["R-LIC-1", "R-LIC-2"], "cmd": ["reuse", "lint"]},
    {"id": "C-COMMIT-MSG", "title": "Commit messages follow .gitmessage",
     "reqs": ["R-PROC-1"],
     "cmd": lambda: [PY, "-I", "tools/check-commit-msg.py", "--range", _commit_range()]},
    {"id": "C-LOW-PROFILE", "title": "Low profile: name, description, topics, README",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-1"], "cmd": _low_profile_cmd},
    {"id": "C-SECRETS", "title": "No secrets in tracked files",
     "reqs": ["R-PUB-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "secrets"]},
    {"id": "C-NO-TOOLCHAIN", "title": "No toolchain parts or binaries tracked",
     "reqs": ["R-REPRO-1"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-tracked.py", "no-toolchain"]},
    {"id": "C-DENY-LISTS", "title": "Claude Code deny lists never drop an entry",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-4", "R-SEP-2"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-deny-lists.py"]},
    {"id": "C-TRANSCRIPTS", "title": "Archived session transcripts: banners and forbidden material",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-1", "R-CLEAN-3", "R-CLEAN-5", "R-SEP-2"],
     "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-transcripts.py"]},
    {"id": "C-SEP-TERMS", "title": "No emulator-only identifiers outside the spec side's folders",
     "reqs": ["R-SEP-1"], "cmd": [PY, "-I", "tools/check-emulator-terms.py"]},
    {"id": "C-CLEAN-FOLDER", "title": "A fresh clean folder has no spec-side files and denies them",
     "reqs": ["R-CLEAN-1", "R-SEP-2"], "needs": "vendor/emulator", "cmd": ["sh", "tools/check-clean-folder.sh"]},

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Spec-side text discipline (R-SEP-1, check C-SEP-TERMS).

  check-emulator-terms.py [--show]

Looks for identifiers that occur in vendor/emulator/ and nowhere in
vendor/jieli-sdk/, in the places the firmware side reads:
  - every tracked text file outside vendor/emulator/, harness/, sessions/
    (transcripts), docs/prompts/ (prompts are kept verbatim), and the two
    doors, docs/HARNESS.md and HARDWARE-SPEC.md (reviewed by people);
  - the commit messages in COMMIT_RANGE (default ..HEAD);
  - the pull request's title and body, when GITHUB_EVENT_PATH names one.

The list is built at run time from vendor/emulator/ and never written down:
identifier-shaped words (with an underscore, inner capitals, or letters and
digits mixed; four characters or more, not just hex digits) and hex numbers
of four digits or more. Terms that already occur in CLEAN_BASELINE's tree
(the repository as the clean side left it at the end of M0a, before any
emulator source entered it) or in vendor/jieli-sdk/ are not on the list. A hit is reported as its place and a SHA-256 prefix of the word, never
the word or the text around it, because the log is visible to the firmware
side; `--show` prints the word too, for a spec-side author fixing it. A
reviewed false positive is listed by that hash in
config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json, with a reason that doesn't name it.

Where vendor/emulator/ isn't on disk (a clean folder), it says SKIP.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
EMU = os.path.join(ROOT, "vendor", "emulator")
SDK = os.path.join(ROOT, "vendor", "jieli-sdk")
REVIEWED = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "emulator-terms-reviewed.json")
# main at the end of M0a (pull request #2): written by the clean side only
CLEAN_BASELINE = "265f15b5b646cf7d5110d4606365d82fae93f5bc"
EXCLUDE = ("vendor/emulator/", "harness/", "sessions/", "docs/prompts/")
DOORS = ("docs/HARNESS.md", "HARDWARE-SPEC.md", "docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md")

WORD = re.compile(r"(?<![0-9A-Za-z_])[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*")
HEX = re.compile(r"\b0[xX][0-9A-Fa-f_]{4,}\b")


def shaped(w):
    if len(w) < 4 or not re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", w):
        return False
    if re.fullmatch(r"x?[0-9A-Fa-f]+(_[ui](8|16|32|64))?", w):
        return False
    if "_" in w.strip("_"):
        return True
    if re.search(r"[a-z][A-Z]", w):
        return True
    return bool(re.search(r"[A-Za-z]", w) and re.search(r"[0-9]", w))


def norm_hex(h):
    v = int(h[2:].replace("_", ""), 16)
    return "0x%x" % v if v >= 0x1000 else None


def terms_of(text):
    out = set(n for n in (norm_hex(h) for h in HEX.findall(text)) if n)
    out.update(w for w in WORD.findall(HEX.sub(" ", text)) if shaped(w))
    return out


def walk_text(top):
    for dirpath, _, names in os.walk(top):
        for n in names:
            try:
                with open(os.path.join(dirpath, n), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    yield f.read()
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
                continue


def emulator_terms():
    emu = set()
    for text in walk_text(EMU):
        emu |= terms_of(text)
    known = set()
    for text in walk_text(SDK):
        known |= terms_of(text)
    for text in baseline_texts():
        known |= terms_of(text)
    return emu - known


def baseline_texts():
    names = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "ls-tree", "-r", "--name-only", CLEAN_BASELINE],
                           check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True).stdout.split()
    for n in names:
        blob = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "show", "%s:%s" % (CLEAN_BASELINE, n)],
                              stdout=subprocess.PIPE).stdout
        try:
            yield blob.decode("utf-8")
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            continue


def h(term):
    return hashlib.sha256(term.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]


def reviewed():
    if not os.path.exists(REVIEWED):
        return {}
    with open(REVIEWED, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data = json.load(f)
    out = {}
    for r in data.get("reviewed", []):
        if not (r.get("sha256_16") and r.get("reason")):
            raise SystemExit("%s: each entry needs sha256_16 and reason" % REVIEWED)
        out[r["sha256_16"]] = r["reason"]
    return out


def tracked():
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "ls-files", "-z"], check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    return [x.decode() for x in p.stdout.split(b"\0") if x]


def hits_in(text, terms, where):
    found = []
    for n, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), 1):
        for t in terms_of(line) & terms:
            found.append((where, n, t))
    return found


def main():
    show = "--show" in sys.argv[1:]
    if not os.path.isdir(EMU):
        print("SKIP: vendor/emulator/ is not on disk (a clean folder leaves it out)")
        return 0
    terms = emulator_terms()
    ok_hashes = reviewed()
    hits = []
    scanned = 0
    for p in tracked():
        if p.startswith(EXCLUDE) or p in DOORS:
            continue
        try:
            with open(os.path.join(ROOT, p), encoding="utf-8") as f:
                text = f.read()
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, OSError):
            continue
        scanned += 1
        hits += hits_in(text, terms, p)
    rng = os.environ.get("COMMIT_RANGE") or "..HEAD"
    log = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", ROOT, "log", "--format=%x00%H%n%B", rng],
                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, universal_newlines=True).stdout
    commits = [c for c in log.split("\0") if c.strip()]
    for c in commits:
        sha, _, body = c.partition("\n")
        hits += hits_in(body, terms, "commit %s" % sha[:12])
    event = os.environ.get("GITHUB_EVENT_PATH")
    pr = 0
    if event and os.path.exists(event):
        with open(event, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            ev = json.load(f)
        pull = ev.get("pull_request") or {}
        if pull:
            pr = 1
            hits += hits_in(pull.get("title") or "", terms, "pull request title")
            hits += hits_in(pull.get("body") or "", terms, "pull request body")
    bad = 0
    for where, n, t in sorted(hits):
        key = h(t)
        if key in ok_hashes:
            print("REVIEWED %s:%d term %s: %s" % (where, n, key, ok_hashes[key]))
            continue
        bad += 1
        print("HIT %s:%d term %s%s" % (where, n, key, (" (%s)" % t) if show else ""))
    print("%d emulator-only terms; %d files, %d commit messages, %d pull request texts scanned"
          % (len(terms), scanned, len(commits), pr))
    print("emulator terms: %s" % ("FAIL" if bad else "PASS"))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

You are the spec-side session for milestone M0b of the small-beeps repository. Read this whole message before starting.

Setup notes for this session:
- You are running in ~/work/small-beeps/spec on the owner's Docker machine. The folder holds only .claude/settings.json, created by hand by the owner before this session started. Never edit, remove or loosen it.
- The owner is driving this from a phone via Remote Control: keep questions short and one at a time. The owner merges PRs with GitHub's merge button; you never merge, and never hold the owner's signing key.
- This prompt deliberately contains no hardware facts, because it will be committed to docs/prompts/, which firmware-side (clean) sessions read.

# M0b: the emulator harness (spec side)

## 0. Get the repo into this folder, and set it up

1. This folder isn't empty, so don't `git clone` into it. Instead: `git init`, add the remote https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps, fetch, and check out `main` (the hand-made .claude/settings.json is untracked and ignored, so it stays).
2. Read CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/PLAN.md (M0b and M0c), docs/EXPOSURE.md, docs/REQUIREMENTS.md and sessions/README.md. They are the rules; this prompt adds to them.
3. Record the hand-made file's SHA-256 in EXPOSURE.md as M0a did for the clean one, then run `tools/spec-setup.sh` (no argument: it sets up this checkout). It must accept the hand-made rules without dropping any. The banner hook takes effect from the next session; record that this session started without it.
4. Archive the previous session (M0a, clean side) with tools/archive-session.py and run tools/check-transcripts.py, as sessions/README.md says. Then add your own entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md: spec side, model ID and its training cutoff, and that you will read the F-Emulator / fm1-emu emulator source (crates fm1-isa, fm1-core, fm1-soc).
5. Save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/M0b.md in your first commit.

## 1. Rules for the spec side

- **You may read** the emulator source in the public upstream `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` (MIT), the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE, datasheets and anything the firmware side may use.
- **You never open, fetch, search or quote** Felucca and anything built on it, dinghy and anything built on it, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` and `probes/lcdtest.c`, or M-VAVE's stock firmware and its disassembly. Even exposed, we don't copy from GPL code: the spec carries facts, never code.
- **Nothing you learn from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/`, except through two doors:** `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (M0c, facts only, each sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (this milestone: the harness's interface, below). The firmware side reads everything else in the repo, so:
  - **commit messages, PR titles and descriptions** from the spec side describe *what changed in the harness* in general terms, never emulator internals (no register names, addresses, struct names, code excerpts). Put that detail in comments inside `harness/` instead;
  - nothing under `docs/`, `tests/` (outside harness), `tools/`, records or release notes may contain emulator internals;
  - CI logs and records from harness runs may show results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), not emulator source.
- **Spec-side transcripts contain emulator source**, so they must never reach a clean folder. Archive them under `sessions/spec/` (move the scheme in tools/archive-session.py, check-transcripts.py and sessions/README.md to `sessions/clean/` and `sessions/spec/`). Add `/sessions/spec/` to the clean sparse-checkout excludes in tools/setup-folder.sh, and add `Read(./sessions/spec/**)` to config/claude/clean.json's deny list (adding a rule is allowed; the deny-list test must keep passing). Make check-transcripts.py skip, not read, spec transcripts that aren't on disk, so it still works in a clean folder.
- **Who archives whom:** a spec session may archive the previous session of either role. A clean session archives only clean sessions and never opens anything under `sessions/spec/`. Write this into sessions/README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.

## 2. Vendor the emulator

- Copy `crates/fm1-isa`, `crates/fm1-core` and `crates/fm1-soc` from the public upstream at a pinned commit (the current main, recorded by hash) into `vendor/emulator/`, with the upstream LICENSE and a `vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md` saying where and which commit. Never bring in anything else from that repo (no `fm1-sid/`, no probes, no other crates, no firmware files).
- A fetch script (`tools/fetch-emulator.sh`) reproduces the copy from the pinned commit and checks a tree hash, like tools/fetch-sdk.sh does for the SDK.
- Keep upstream code unmodified. If the harness needs a change in it, make the smallest patch, keep it as a separate file under `vendor/emulator/patches/`, apply it in the fetch script, and say why in UPSTREAM.md.
- REUSE: vendored files keep upstream's licence (add REUSE.toml entries as needed). PROVENANCE.md logs the vendoring.

## 3. The harness

`harness/`: a Rust workspace (Rust toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml; Cargo.lock committed; third-party crates checked by the lockfile's hashes), a library plus the `fwtest` CLI. It must:
- boot a raw firmware image (no M-VAVE loaders, nothing M-VAVE's), with the image format and load rules written down in docs/HARNESS.md as the firmware side will need them;
- run N emulated milliseconds, driving inputs from a timed script (keys, encoders, the pot, MIDI in) in a simple text format;
- capture, as asked: RAM regions, the LCD as PNG, LED states, flash contents, audio as WAV, and instructions executed per audio block;
- detect halts, faults and hangs, and say which with a clear exit code;
- compare outputs with golden files (exact for deterministic outputs; documented tolerances where an output is meant to be approximate);
- emit JUnit XML and JSON results that tools/record.py can include in the commit's record.

Determinism: the same image, script and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs on every run and every machine. Test that in CI by running twice.

Harness tests: tiny test images for the harness's own tests live in `harness/tests/` (spec side, excluded from clean). Write them from the emulator's documented behaviour, not from any probe or firmware in fm1-emu.

## 4. How the firmware side uses it without seeing it

The clean side never has harness or emulator source on disk, so it uses a prebuilt fwtest:
- CI builds a container image with fwtest from `main` (base image pinned by digest, deterministic build) and publishes it to GHCR under the repo's name, low profile (no quiet words in the image name, labels or description).
- `tools/fwtest` (outside harness/, so the clean side has it) runs that image **pinned by digest**. The digest lives in a small committed file updated by a PR whenever the harness changes.
- docs/HARNESS.md is the clean side's whole manual: the CLI, the input-script format, outputs, exit codes, golden-file rules and the raw-image format. It describes behaviour as a black box; it doesn't explain how the emulator works inside. Review it against the rules in section 1 before committing.
- Records: when firmware tests run fwtest, the record notes the image digest used.

## 5. The spec-request channel

Create `docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md`: how the firmware side asks for a hardware fact (a numbered question, why it's needed, the date), and how the spec side answers (by adding a sourced fact to HARDWARE-SPEC.md and linking it, never with code or explanations of other firmwares). Empty for now apart from the instructions and a template.

## 6. Requirements and plan

- Add R-HARN-* requirements (boot, inputs, each capture, halts, golden files, determinism, results format, the clean-side wrapper) to docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, each traced to tests.
- Add requirements for the separation itself: spec-side text discipline (section 1), sessions/spec exclusion, and that tools/fwtest uses a pinned image digest. Add CI checks where they can be automated (e.g. a check that commit messages and docs outside harness/ contain no identifiers that appear only in vendor/emulator/: build the list of such identifiers automatically and report hits without printing surrounding source).
- Update docs/PLAN.md: M0b's actual results; M0c next (spec side).

## Done when

- The repo is set up in this folder with the spec config and banner hook; the M0a transcript is archived and checked; EXPOSURE.md has this session's entry.
- `vendor/emulator/` is reproducible from the pinned upstream commit by script and hash.
- `fwtest` builds in the pinned container; its own tests pass in CI and run twice with identical outputs; JUnit/JSON results land in the commit's record.
- The fwtest image is published by digest, and `tools/fwtest` runs it.
- A fresh clean folder made with `tools/clean-setup.sh <new dir>` contains no `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` or `sessions/spec/`, and its settings deny them. Test this in CI.
- docs/HARNESS.md and docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md exist and pass review against section 1.
- Work arrives as small commits in one or more PRs, each with the What/Why/How/Result template; the owner merges them with the button.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Don't archive your own transcript; the next session does.

# M0b: the emulator harness (spec side)

## 0. Get the repo into this folder, and set it up

1. This folder isn't empty, so don't `git clone` into it. Instead: `git init`, add the remote https://github.com/japes98/small-beeps, fetch, and check out `main` (the hand-made .claude/settings.json is untracked and ignored, so it stays).

3. Record the hand-made file's SHA-256 in EXPOSURE.md as M0a did for the clean one, then run `tools/spec-setup.sh` (no argument: it sets up this checkout). It must accept the hand-made rules without dropping any. The banner hook takes effect from the next session; record that this session started without it.
4. Archive the previous session (M0a, clean side) with tools/archive-session.py and run tools/check-transcripts.py, as sessions/README.md says. Then add your own entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md: spec side, model ID and its training cutoff, and that you will read the F-Emulator / fm1-emu emulator source (crates fm1-isa, fm1-core, fm1-soc).
5. Save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/M0b.md in your first commit.

## 1. Rules for the spec side

- **You may read** the emulator source in the public upstream `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` (MIT), the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE, datasheets and anything the firmware side may use.
- **You never open, fetch, search or quote** Felucca and anything built on it, dinghy and anything built on it, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` and `probes/lcdtest.c`, or M-VAVE's stock firmware and its disassembly. Even exposed, we don't copy from GPL code: the spec carries facts, never code.
- **Nothing you learn from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/`, except through two doors:** `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (M0c, facts only, each sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (this milestone: the harness's interface, below). The firmware side reads everything else in the repo, so:
  - **commit messages, PR titles and descriptions** from the spec side describe *what changed in the harness* in general terms, never emulator internals (no register names, addresses, struct names, code excerpts). Put that detail in comments inside `harness/` instead;
  - nothing under `docs/`, `tests/` (outside harness), `tools/`, records or release notes may contain emulator internals;
  - CI logs and records from harness runs may show results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), not emulator source.
- **Spec-side transcripts contain emulator source**, so they must never reach a clean folder. Archive them under `sessions/spec/` (move the scheme in tools/archive-session.py, check-transcripts.py and sessions/README.md to `sessions/clean/` and `sessions/spec/`). Add `/sessions/spec/` to the clean sparse-checkout excludes in tools/setup-folder.sh, and add `Read(./sessions/spec/**)` to config/claude/clean.json's deny list (adding a rule is allowed; the deny-list test must keep passing). Make check-transcripts.py skip, not read, spec transcripts that aren't on disk, so it still works in a clean folder.
- **Who archives whom:** a spec session may archive the previous session of either role. A clean session archives only clean sessions and never opens anything under `sessions/spec/`. Write this into sessions/README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.

## 2. Vendor the emulator

- Copy `crates/fm1-isa`, `crates/fm1-core` and `crates/fm1-soc` from the public upstream at a pinned commit (the current main, recorded by hash) into `vendor/emulator/`, with the upstream LICENSE and a `vendor/emulator/UPSTREAM.md` saying where and which commit. Never bring in anything else from that repo (no `fm1-sid/`, no probes, no other crates, no firmware files).
- A fetch script (`tools/fetch-emulator.sh`) reproduces the copy from the pinned commit and checks a tree hash, like tools/fetch-sdk.sh does for the SDK.
- Keep upstream code unmodified. If the harness needs a change in it, make the smallest patch, keep it as a separate file under `vendor/emulator/patches/`, apply it in the fetch script, and say why in UPSTREAM.md.
- REUSE: vendored files keep upstream's licence (add REUSE.toml entries as needed). PROVENANCE.md logs the vendoring.

## 3. The harness

`harness/`: a Rust workspace (Rust toolchain pinned in rust-toolchain.toml; Cargo.lock committed; third-party crates checked by the lockfile's hashes), a library plus the `fwtest` CLI. It must:
- boot a raw firmware image (no M-VAVE loaders, nothing M-VAVE's), with the image format and load rules written down in docs/HARNESS.md as the firmware side will need them;
- run N emulated milliseconds, driving inputs from a timed script (keys, encoders, the pot, MIDI in) in a simple text format;
- capture, as asked: RAM regions, the LCD as PNG, LED states, flash contents, audio as WAV, and instructions executed per audio block;
- detect halts, faults and hangs, and say which with a clear exit code;
- compare outputs with golden files (exact for deterministic outputs; documented tolerances where an output is meant to be approximate);
- emit JUnit XML and JSON results that tools/record.py can include in the commit's record.

Determinism: the same image, script and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs on every run and every machine. Test that in CI by running twice.

Harness tests: tiny test images for the harness's own tests live in `harness/tests/` (spec side, excluded from clean). Write them from the emulator's documented behaviour, not from any probe or firmware in fm1-emu.

## 4. How the firmware side uses it without seeing it

The clean side never has harness or emulator source on disk, so it uses a prebuilt fwtest:
- CI builds a container image with fwtest from `main` (base image pinned by digest, deterministic build) and publishes it to GHCR under the repo's name, low profile (no quiet words in the image name, labels or description).
- `tools/fwtest` (outside harness/, so the clean side has it) runs that image **pinned by digest**. The digest lives in a small committed file updated by a PR whenever the harness changes.
- docs/HARNESS.md is the clean side's whole manual: the CLI, the input-script format, outputs, exit codes, golden-file rules and the raw-image format. It describes behaviour as a black box; it doesn't explain how the emulator works inside. Review it against the rules in section 1 before committing.
- Records: when firmware tests run fwtest, the record notes the image digest used.

## 5. The spec-request channel

Create `docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md`: how the firmware side asks for a hardware fact (a numbered question, why it's needed, the date), and how the spec side answers (by adding a sourced fact to HARDWARE-SPEC.md and linking it, never with code or explanations of other firmwares). Empty for now apart from the instructions and a template.

## 6. Requirements and plan

- Add R-HARN-* requirements (boot, inputs, each capture, halts, golden files, determinism, results format, the clean-side wrapper) to docs/REQUIREMENTS.md, each traced to tests.
- Add requirements for the separation itself: spec-side text discipline (section 1), sessions/spec exclusion, and that tools/fwtest uses a pinned image digest. Add CI checks where they can be automated (e.g. a check that commit messages and docs outside harness/ contain no identifiers that appear only in vendor/emulator/: build the list of such identifiers automatically and report hits without printing surrounding source).
- Update docs/PLAN.md: M0b's actual results; M0c next (spec side).

- The fwtest image is published by digest, and `tools/fwtest` runs it.
- A fresh clean folder made with `tools/clean-setup.sh <new dir>` contains no `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` or `sessions/spec/`, and its settings deny them. Test this in CI.
- docs/HARNESS.md and docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md exist and pass review against section 1.
- Work arrives as small commits in one or more PRs, each with the What/Why/How/Result template; the owner merges them with the button.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Don't archive your own transcript; the next session does.

import json
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

ar = load_tool("archive-session.py")
ct = load_tool("check-transcripts.py")

# Built at run time so this file never contains a token-shaped string.
TOKEN = "gh" + "o_" + "A1b2C3d4" * 5
KEY = "sk-" + "ant-" + "x" * 30
PRIVATE = ("-----BEGIN OPENSSH " + "PRIVATE KEY-----\\nabc\\n-----END OPENSSH "
           + "PRIVATE KEY-----")


class ArchiveTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-CLEAN-3"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def test_redact_line(self):
        counts = {}
        line = json.dumps({
            "text": "token %s key %s mail [REDACTED:email] keep noreply@anthropic.com "
                    "path ~/Development/x tmp /tmp/claude-UID/a"
                    % (TOKEN, KEY),
            "ownerAccountUuid": "abc-123"}) + "\n"
        line = line.replace("PLACEHOLDER", "")
        out = ar.redact_line(line, counts)
        json.loads(out)
        for gone in (TOKEN, KEY, "[REDACTED:email]", "~", "claude-501", "abc-123"):
            self.assertNotIn(gone, out)
        self.assertIn("noreply@anthropic.com", out)
        self.assertIn("~/Development/x", out)

    def test_private_key_in_json_string(self):
        line = json.dumps({"t": "x"}).replace('"x"', '"%s"' % PRIVATE) + "\n"
        counts = {}
        out = ar.redact_line(line, counts)
        self.assertNotIn("PRIVATE KEY-----\\nabc", out)
        json.loads(out)

    def test_archive_end_to_end_then_check(self):
        sid = "aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee"
        src_dir = os.path.join(self.dir, "projects")
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(src_dir, sid, "subagents"))
        src = os.path.join(src_dir, sid + ".jsonl")
        banner = ("=== small-beeps session banner v1 ===\nstatus: OK\n")
        with open(src, "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "attachment", "timestamp": "2026-10-22T01:02:03Z",
                                "attachment": {"hookEvent": "SessionStart", "exitCode": 0,
                                               "stdout": banner}}) + "\n")

You are the spec-side session for milestone M0c of the small-beeps repository. Read this whole message before starting.

Setup notes for this session:
- You are in ~/Development/[REDACTED:private]/spec, set up by M0b with the spec config and banner. The owner drives this from a phone via Remote Control: short questions, one at a time. The owner merges PRs with GitHub's merge button.
- This prompt deliberately contains no hardware facts, because it is committed to docs/prompts/, which firmware-side sessions read.

# M0c: HARDWARE-SPEC.md (spec side)

## 0. Start

1. Update to main. Archive the previous spec session (M0b) into sessions/spec/ with tools/archive-session.py, and run tools/check-transcripts.py, as sessions/README.md says. Also archive any clean session that ended since the last archive (a short clean maintenance session that updated the clean folder).
2. Add your entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md (spec side, model ID and cutoff, what you will read).
3. Save this prompt unedited as docs/prompts/M0c.md in your first commit.

## 1. What HARDWARE-SPEC.md is

The firmware side's only window onto what the spec side knows. It holds facts about the hardware and about how fwtest presents it, never code and never how any firmware or the emulator is written. It is read by people and agents who must stay clean, so treat every line as if it will be read in court.

Every fact is an entry:
- an ID (HW-1, HW-2, ...; never reused or renumbered; a corrected fact gets a new ID and the old one is marked superseded, not deleted);
- the fact, stated as a property of the hardware or a requirement it imposes ("bit N of register R enables X"; "after reset, the LCD needs at least T ms before the first command"), never as a procedure copied from code;
- its sources, as precisely as possible (file and line or section of the JieLi SDK at the vendored commit, FM-1-RE document and section, datasheet and page, or "black-box experiment E-n");
- its standing: **confirmed** (an independent non-GPL source, or a spec-side black-box experiment in fwtest, agrees), or **emulator-only** (the only source is the emulator model, which was partly written from GPL code; the firmware side may rely on it but should prefer to confirm it by its own black-box test).

## 2. Rules for writing it

- Names: use the JieLi SDK's names for registers, bits and peripherals wherever they exist. Otherwise use plain descriptive names. Never use identifiers that occur only in vendor/emulator/ (CI's separation check will catch them).
- Facts, not code: no code, pseudo-code, struct layouts, tables copied from source, or comments copied from anywhere. No initialisation sequences transcribed from the emulator or the SDK's driver code: state the requirements (what must be set, what order is required by the hardware, timing limits) and let the firmware side design its own sequence.
- Minimal: include what the firmware side needs for M0d through M4 (below), and the answers to any open spec requests. Don't dump everything the emulator models. More can be added later through spec requests.
- Never derive a fact from forbidden material (Felucca and its descendants, dinghy, fm1-sid, probes/lcdtest.c, stock firmware or its disassembly), even indirectly. If the only way to learn something would be from those, record it as an open question, not a fact.
- Black-box experiments: you may confirm facts by writing small spec-side test images that you run in fwtest. They live under harness/spec-experiments/ (excluded from clean folders; add that path to the separation checks if needed). In the spec, cite them only by ID (E-n) and result ("E-4: writing X made Y happen within T"); their code never leaves harness/.

## 3. What it must cover

Organised by subsystem, each section saying which milestone needs it:
- the raw image and boot as fwtest presents them (consistent with docs/HARNESS.md, which defers some of this to the spec): load address, entry, the memories and their sizes, what state the core is in at entry, and how the second core is released;
- clocks and timers, and interrupts (enough for M1);
- the debug/marker channel fwtest observes;
- the LCD and its interface (M2);
- keys, the key matrix, encoders, the pot and LEDs, including the mapping from fwtest's key, LED and encoder numbers to the panel (M3);
- audio output: format, rate, how samples reach the output, and the timing fwtest measures (M4);
- flash storage, only as far as M7 will need; mark it later if it isn't ready;
- open questions: what isn't known, or is known only from forbidden material.

## 4. Review before the firmware side reads it

- When the draft is complete, start a fresh subagent with no context except docs/HARDWARE-SPEC.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and sections 1 and 2 of this prompt, and have it review every entry for: code or procedure-from-code, emulator-only identifiers, missing or vague sources, facts that seem to come from forbidden material, and anything the firmware side couldn't act on. Fix what it finds; commit its report as docs/reviews/M0c-spec-review.md.
- Run the separation checks over the spec. Add HARDWARE-SPEC.md to any check that should cover it.
- Add R-SPEC-* requirements (every entry has a source and a standing; no emulator-only identifiers; reviewed before release to the clean side) with tests where they can be automated, e.g. a lint that parses entries and fails on a missing ID, source or standing.

## Done when

- HARDWARE-SPEC.md covers section 3, every entry sourced with a standing, open questions listed.
- The review report is committed and its findings fixed; the separation checks and spec lint pass in CI; the record is PASS.
- docs/PLAN.md has M0c's results and says M0d (clean side) is next.
- PRs are small, follow the commit template, and say nothing about emulator internals outside harness/.
- Finish by committing everything and telling the owner "done, ready to clear". Don't archive your own transcript.

# Addendum (part of M0c)

1. When you archive the clean maintenance session, redact the merge summary's lines that list paths under vendor/emulator/ and harness/ (replace them with a note), and say so in its REDACTIONS.md. The owner keeps the original.
2. Fix the cause: in tools/clean-update.sh and the steps in docs/PLAN.md, the merge must run with --no-stat (and -q), because a diffstat lazily fetches the blobs it counts. Add a CI test that updates a blob-less sparse clean clone across a commit that changes vendor/emulator/ and harness/, and checks that none of their blobs reach .git.

class ArchiveTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-CLEAN-3"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def test_redact_line(self):
        counts = {}
        line = json.dumps({
            "text": "token %s key %s mail [REDACTED:email] keep noreply@anthropic.com "
                    "path ~/Development/x tmp /tmp/claude-UID/a"
                    % (TOKEN, KEY),
            "ownerAccountUuid": "abc-123"}) + "\n"
        line = line.replace("PLACEHOLDER", "")
        out = ar.redact_line(line, counts)
        json.loads(out)
        for gone in (TOKEN, KEY, "[REDACTED:email]", "~", "claude-501", "abc-123"):
            self.assertNotIn(gone, out)
        self.assertIn("noreply@anthropic.com", out)
        self.assertIn("~/Development/x", out)

    def test_private_key_in_json_string(self):
        line = json.dumps({"t": "x"}).replace('"x"', '"%s"' % PRIVATE) + "\n"
        counts = {}

        self.assertNotIn("PRIVATE KEY-----\\nabc", out)
        json.loads(out)

        with open(src, "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "attachment", "timestamp": "2026-10-22T01:02:03Z",
                                "attachment": {"hookEvent": "SessionStart", "exitCode": 0,

            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "user", "message": {"content": "hi " + TOKEN}}) + "\n")
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "user", "message": {"content":
                "cwd ~/x; drwxr-xr-x 3 [REDACTED:user] staff; host [REDACTED:host]"}}) + "\n")
        with open(os.path.join(src_dir, sid, "subagents", "agent-a.jsonl"), "w") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps({"type": "assistant", "message": {"content": []}}) + "\n")

# Plan

An original, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 pocket
synthesizer (JieLi AC791N: two pi32v2 cores, 240x240 LCD, key matrix, rotary
encoders, I2S audio), written clean-room so it can ship inside the
F-Emulator iOS app, provably independent of the FM-1's GPL community
firmwares.

Each milestone has its own prompt (`docs/prompts/<Mx>.md`) and its own fresh
session. Roles are defined in CONTRIBUTING.md; requirement IDs are in
docs/REQUIREMENTS.md.

## Milestones

### M0a: foundation (firmware side)
Repo, rules, roles, exposure register, records, signing, toolchain, SDK, CI.
No firmware code yet; a placeholder translation unit proves the pipeline.
- Requirements: R-PROC-1..4, R-REC-1..2, R-REPRO-1..5, R-BUILD-1,
  R-LIC-1..2, R-PUB-1..2, R-CLEAN-1..5.
- Done when: the repo exists with the bootstrap commit and rulesets; CI on a
  pull request runs reuse lint, the commit-message check, the low-profile
  check, the toolchain container build with its checksum and the
  byte-for-byte double build; the owner's signed merge produces the first
  record with a pending OpenTimestamps proof; `tools/reproduce` works;
  EXPOSURE.md and PROVENANCE.md are complete; nothing forbidden was opened.
- Status 2026-10-22: pull request #1 merged as `2fd28219`. Its record
  (`records/2fd28219…/` on `records`) has 13 checks PASS and C-MERGE FAIL
  under the merge rule of the time (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge policy and its
  history"), with a pending OpenTimestamps proof (three calendars).
  `tools/reproduce 2fd28219` on the owner's Mac: REPRODUCED (both outputs
  match the record).

### M0b: harness (spec side)
Vendor the emulator crates `fm1-isa`, `fm1-core`, `fm1-soc` from the public
upstream `joakimeriksson/fm1-emu` at a pinned commit, with its MIT licence,
into `vendor/emulator/` (never the rest of that repo). Build the harness: a
Rust library and `fwtest` CLI that boots a raw image, runs N emulated ms with
a timed input script, captures RAM, the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV)
and instructions per audio block, detects halts, compares golden files, and
emits JUnit and JSON.
- Requirements: R-REPRO-*, R-LIC-*, new harness requirements (R-HARN-*).
- Done when: `fwtest` runs in CI from a pinned container, its outputs are
  deterministic, and `tools/clean-setup.sh` excludes `vendor/emulator/` and
  `harness/` from clean clones.
- Status 2026-10-22 (session M0b, spec side, on the owner's Mac):
  - **Setup** (pull request #3): the spec folder, its hand-made settings kept
    and guarded, M0a's transcripts archived in `sessions/clean/`; spec-side
    transcripts go to `sessions/spec/`, which clean folders leave out and
    deny (R-SEP-2).
  - **Emulator** (pull request #4): three crates vendored at upstream commit
    `43ed5580`, reproducible by `tools/fetch-emulator.sh` with a tree hash
    (C-EMU-PIN). One patch, to the workspace manifest only.
  - **Harness** (pull request #4): `fwtest`, a Rust library and CLI with no
    third-party crates, built offline in a container on digest-pinned bases
    (Rust 1.99.0). It boots raw images, takes timed inputs, captures RAM,
    the LCD (PNG), LEDs, flash, audio (WAV), instructions per audio block
    and the debug console, tells faults, halts and hangs apart, compares
    golden files, and writes JSON and JUnit. Its own tests: 23 cargo tests
    and a 13-case suite on 12 small test images built with the pinned
    toolchain. The suite's outputs were byte-identical in two amd64
    containers at different paths and on Apple Silicon natively.
  - **Separation**: docs/HARNESS.md (the clean side's manual) and
    docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md; checks C-SEP-TERMS, C-CLEAN-FOLDER and
    C-FWTEST-PIN; requirements R-SEP-1..3 and R-HARN-1..10.
  - **Merged**: #3 as `0ad38801`, #4 as `5d4d6fd2`. The records for both
    merges are PASS, with every check run, none skipped. The second
    record's `harness/` holds the suite's JSON, JUnit and output hashes.
  - **Publishing**: `.github/workflows/fwtest-image.yml` pushed the image
    built from `5d4d6fd2` as
    `ghcr.io/japes98/small-beeps@sha256:fa74baf9…` (public; pulls without
    logging in). `config/fwtest-image` pins it, and the suite run through
    `tools/fwtest` with it gives all 47 output files with the same SHA-256
    as that record.
  - **Before the next clean session**, in the clean folder, from a shell:
    `export GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1; git fetch origin;` then
    `env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git merge -q --no-stat --ff-only origin/main`
    (only the folder's own files are fetched; without `--no-stat` the merge
    summary downloads the excluded files to count their lines, as
    happened in clean maintenance session 1), then `tools/clean-setup.sh`. Its live
    settings predate the new deny rule and the lazy-fetch setting, so its
    banner would otherwise say CONFIG MISMATCH. From then on,
    `tools/clean-update.sh` updates it.

### M0c: hardware spec (spec side, next)
`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols),
each with its source. Facts whose only source is the emulator are marked as
such. It also maps fwtest's key, LED and encoder numbers to the panel and
the key matrix, and covers what docs/HARNESS.md defers to it (the memories,
the second core's release, the audio output's format and rate, the debug
message register), and answers any open spec requests.
- Done when: reviewed for "facts, not code" before the firmware side reads it.

### M0d: smallest firmware (firmware side)
Startup, linker script and `main` (a marker word, a heartbeat), written only
from `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the SDK and FM-1-RE's documents; booted and checked
with `fwtest`. Design choices explained in docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md.
- Requirements: R-BOOT-1, R-BOOT-2, R-BUILD-1.
- Done when: CI boots the image in the harness and the record shows the
  marker word and heartbeat.

### M0e: audit and performance
- **Similarity audit** (spec side): an isolated CI job fetches the GPL
  firmwares at pinned commits, compares our firmware against them with JPlag
  (SDK as base code, `vendor/` excluded, an unrelated permissive embedded C
  project scored as a control), and publishes scores and file names only.
- **Performance tracking** (firmware side): per-commit size and RAM, later
  emulated instructions per audio block. A 3% regression gate on
  instructions per audio block; per-milestone budgets for size and RAM,
  raised only by a pull request that says why.
- Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-PERF-1, R-PERF-2.

### M1 to M9 (firmware side)
- **M1** boot: clocks, interrupts, timer.
- **M2** screen.
- **M3** keys, encoders, pot, LEDs.
- **M4** audio.
- **M5** the FM engine.
- **M6** MIDI in.
- **M7** flash storage.
- **M8** UI and original presets (no Yamaha factory voices).
- **M9** packaging, and a raw-image boot path in the app.

### Level 2: real hardware
- **M10** recovery kit.
- **M11** USB-MIDI and the update handler.
- **M12** hardware checklist.

## Risks

- **The toolchain's availability and terms.** JieLi's Linux toolchain has no
  licence file (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md). We never redistribute it. If the
  download disappears, a full rebuild needs another copy (the private
  preservation repo), but every released binary stays verifiable by its
  recorded hash. The vendor's short link already points at a newer release
  (20260730.1) than the pinned one; the pinned file is fetched by its direct
  URL.
- **Packages for real hardware.** A `.fwsc` package may need M-VAVE's boot or
  update loader, which we can't redistribute. Find out from FM-1-RE's
  documents only, before M9, and record the answer here. The app is
  unaffected (it can boot our raw image). *Answer: not yet investigated.*
- **The emulator doesn't model USB**, so M11 is hardware-only.
- **Merge signatures are GitHub's.** Since 2026-10-22 the owner merges with
  GitHub's button, so merge commits are signed by GitHub (`web-flow`) and the
  owner's identity rests on GitHub's `merged_by` record, checked by C-MERGE.
  Milestone tags carry the owner's own SSH signature. The first merge's
  record shows C-MERGE FAIL under the earlier rule (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Merge
  policy and its history").

input.new_string:
no_blobs "after an update"
    clean=$clean_saved
fi

# An update across a commit that changes vendor/emulator/ and harness/. The
# commit is made here, on top of HEAD: in each folder one existing file gets
# new contents and one file is added (made-up text; nothing is read from the
# folders but one file name each). tools/clean-update.sh must bring none of
# their blobs, old or new, into .git. As a control, a plain fast-forward,
# whose merge summary counts the changed files' lines, must fetch some in
# another copy; otherwise this test would prove nothing. The control's output
# goes to /dev/null, since it names the files.
src="$work/src.git"
idx="$work/probe.index"
GIT_INDEX_FILE=$idx git -C "$src" read-tree "$head"
for p in vendor/emulator harness; do
    set -- $(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $1, $4; exit }')
    changed=$(printf 'clean-update probe: %s, changed\n' "$p" | git -C "$src" hash-object -w --stdin)
    added=$(printf 'clean-update probe: %s, added\nsecond line\n' "$p" | git -C "$src" hash-object -w --stdin)
    GIT_INDEX_FILE=$idx git -C "$src" update-index --add --cacheinfo "$1,$changed,$2" \
        --cacheinfo "100644,$added,$p/clean-update-probe.txt"
done
probe=$(git -C "$src" -c user.name=probe -c user.email=probe@invalid commit-tree \
    "$(GIT_INDEX_FILE=$idx git -C "$src" write-tree)" -p "$head" -m "probe: change both folders")
git -C "$src" update-ref refs/heads/main "$probe"
# Every blob under the two folders at HEAD or at the probe commit.
probe_blobs=$( (git -C "$src" ls-tree -r "$head" -- vendor/emulator harness
                git -C "$src" ls-tree -r "$probe" -- vendor/emulator harness) | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' | sort -u)
present() {
    n=0
    for oid in $probe_blobs; do
        if GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$1" cat-file -e "$oid" 2>/dev/null; then n=$((n + 1)); fi
    done
    echo $n
}
for c in probe-update probe-control; do
    SETUP_SOURCE="file://$src" SETUP_REF=checked \
        sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" "$work/$c" > /dev/null 2>&1 || bad "clean-setup.sh for $c failed"
done
if sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-update.sh" --dir "$work/probe-update" main > "$work/probe.log" 2>&1; then
    echo "update across a change to both folders: $(tail -1 "$work/probe.log")"
else
    cat "$work/probe.log"; bad "tools/clean-update.sh across a change to both folders failed"
fi
[ "$(git -C "$work/probe-update" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$probe" ] || bad "the update did not reach the probe commit"
n=$(present "$work/probe-update")
if [ "$n" = 0 ]; then echo "no blobs (update across a change to both folders): 0 present"
else bad "the update across a change to both folders brought $n of their blobs into .git"; fi
GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$work/probe-control" fetch -q origin
env -u GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH git -C "$work/probe-control" merge --ff-only origin/main > /dev/null 2>&1 || true
n=$(present "$work/probe-control")
if [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; then echo "control: a merge with its summary fetched $n of their blobs, as expected"
else bad "control: a merge with its summary fetched none of their blobs, so this test can't tell"; fi

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# C-CLEAN-FOLDER (R-CLEAN-1, R-SEP-2): makes a fresh clean folder with
# tools/clean-setup.sh from this checkout's HEAD, and checks that
#   - vendor/emulator/, harness/ and sessions/spec/ are not on disk;
#   - none of their files' contents are in its .git (a blob-less clone that
#     never fetched them);
#   - its live settings are config/claude/clean.json, which denies reading
#     all three, and the session banner says OK;
#   - its .git/info/attributes marks all three -diff.
#   - the firmware side's own tools, run inside it with git's lazy fetching
#     off as clean sessions run (the tool tests, the transcript and term
#     checks, the emulator pin check, and `git log -p` over this branch,
#     which must fail rather than fetch), fetch none of those contents;
#   - tools/clean-update.sh brings a clean folder made at HEAD's parent up to
#     HEAD with the same results.
# It never reads those folders' contents itself: only their file lists and
# object IDs, from this checkout's history. In a clean folder it says SKIP
# and does nothing: it needs the full history to serve the copy it checks.
set -eu

ROOT=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
if [ ! -d "$ROOT/vendor/emulator" ] || [ "$(cat "$ROOT/.claude/small-beeps-role" 2>/dev/null)" = clean ]; then
    echo "SKIP: this is a clean folder (it can't serve the spec-side files a check would need)"
    exit 0
fi
EXCLUDED="vendor/emulator harness sessions/spec"
work=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail=0
bad() { echo "FAIL: $*"; fail=1; }

head=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse HEAD)
# A bare copy that serves partial clones (a plain local clone would copy every
# object and ignore --filter).
git clone -q --bare --no-local "$ROOT" "$work/src.git"
git -C "$work/src.git" config uploadpack.allowFilter true
git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/checked "$head"

SETUP_SOURCE="file://$work/src.git" SETUP_REF=checked \
    sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" "$work/clean" > "$work/setup.log" 2>&1 || {
    cat "$work/setup.log"; bad "tools/clean-setup.sh failed"; exit 1; }
clean="$work/clean"
[ "$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$head" ] || bad "the clean folder is not at $head"

for p in $EXCLUDED; do
    if [ -e "$clean/$p" ]; then bad "$p is on disk"; else echo "absent:   $p"; fi
done

# Every blob under the excluded paths at HEAD must be missing from the clean
# folder's objects (checked without fetching: --missing=print lists them).
no_blobs() {
    missing=$(git -C "$clean" rev-list --objects --missing=print HEAD -- $EXCLUDED | sed -n 's/^?//p' | sort -u)
    for p in $EXCLUDED; do
        for oid in $(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | awk '$2 == "blob" { print $3 }' | sort -u); do
            if ! printf '%s\n' "$missing" | grep -qx "$oid"; then
                bad "$1: a blob under $p is in the clean folder's .git ($oid)"
            fi
        done
        n=$(git -C "$ROOT" ls-tree -r HEAD -- "$p" | grep -c . || true)
        echo "no blobs ($1): $p ($n files at HEAD)"
    done
}
no_blobs "after setup"

live="$clean/.claude/settings.json"
if cmp -s "$live" "$ROOT/config/claude/clean.json"; then echo "settings: config/claude/clean.json"
else bad "the live settings are not config/claude/clean.json"; fi
for rule in 'Read(./vendor/emulator/**)' 'Read(./harness/**)' 'Read(./sessions/spec/**)'; do
    if grep -qF "\"$rule\"" "$live"; then echo "denied:   $rule"; else bad "settings lack $rule"; fi
done
attrs="$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/info/attributes"
for p in $EXCLUDED; do
    grep -qxF "/$p/** -diff" "$attrs" || bad "$attrs lacks /$p/** -diff"
done
grep -q '^status: OK' "$work/setup.log" || bad "the banner did not say status: OK"

# The firmware side's tools, run inside the clean folder, must not fetch them.
py=$(sh "$ROOT/tools/find-python.sh")
base=$(git -C "$ROOT" merge-base HEAD "$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --verify -q origin/main || echo HEAD)")
(cd "$clean" && GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 COMMIT_RANGE="$base..HEAD" "$py" tools/record.py run --out "$work/inside" \
    --only C-UNIT,C-TRANSCRIPTS,C-SEP-TERMS,C-EMU-PIN,C-CLEAN-FOLDER,C-FWTEST-PIN) > "$work/inside.log" 2>&1 \
    || { cat "$work/inside.log"; bad "the firmware side's checks failed inside the clean folder"; }
grep -E '^C-' "$work/inside.log" | sed 's/^/inside:   /'
if GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 git -C "$clean" log -p "$base..HEAD" > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "git log -p: needed no excluded file"
else
    echo "git log -p: refused to fetch excluded files, as it should"
fi
no_blobs "after the tools and git log -p"

# An update from HEAD's parent to HEAD.
if parent=$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse -q --verify "HEAD~1"); then
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/old "$parent"
    git -C "$work/src.git" update-ref refs/heads/main "$head"
    SETUP_SOURCE="file://$work/src.git" SETUP_REF=old \
        sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-setup.sh" "$work/clean2" > /dev/null 2>&1 || bad "clean-setup.sh at HEAD's parent failed"
    if sh "$ROOT/tools/clean-update.sh" --dir "$work/clean2" main > "$work/update.log" 2>&1; then
        echo "update:   $(tail -1 "$work/update.log")"
    else
        cat "$work/update.log"; bad "tools/clean-update.sh failed"
    fi
    clean_saved=$clean; clean="$work/clean2"
    [ "$(git -C "$clean" rev-parse HEAD)" = "$head" ] || bad "the update did not reach HEAD"
    for p in $EXCLUDED; do [ ! -e "$clean/$p" ] || bad "$p is on disk after the update"; done
    no_blobs "after an update"
    clean=$clean_saved
fi

if [ $fail -eq 0 ]; then echo "clean folder: PASS"; else echo "clean folder: FAIL"; fi
exit $fail
